title: Core's sampling law on the device: a draw per logits row by Core's rules and Philox draws, rejection-sampling verify predictions and log-probabilities; an exact top-64 fast path and the full-vocabulary law by prefix searches, spread over several blocks a row

fast-law.what: the fast path (sample, verify): stage blocks of 256 threads x 16 logits a row, each block's exact top 65 packed keys (value descending, id ascending, no atomics) and its FP64 weight partials, then a law block a row merging them in block order and running Core's steps 7 to 12 in FP64 on the candidates; greedy rows, 1 <= top_k <= 64 and the open rows whose kept set closes within the candidates. Its block sizes set the FP64 sums' grouping, so they are fixed: no knobs

yardstick.library: torch ops: argmax for greedy rows (torch.argmax, the lower id on ties as torch takes the first)

full-law.what: the full-vocabulary law of the rows the fast path leaves (one block of 1,024 threads a row): Core's processing into FP32 values, prefix searches over the keys' eight 4-bit digits (per-thread FP32 sums over a fixed stride, FP64 over the warps in order) and the boundary key's ties in id order (the tiles holding a token of it only), the draw; untuned (its order is its block's)

spread-law.what: the full law spread over PARTS blocks a row of a cooperative launch (where the device runs one and the occupancy API says the grid fits; else full-law): the 1,024 threads as virtual threads, every per-thread sum and warp tree the one-block law's, the cross-warp steps through slots in scratch and a per-row barrier, so the full law's bits; CRIT_SAMPLING_ONE_BLOCK=1 takes full-law

PARTS.what: blocks a row's 1,024 threads spread over (whole warps a block: 128, 64 or 32 threads): more of the GPU's multiprocessors for a row against more rows' blocks resident at once; no bit changes
